wu: Warm-up: 'Two Truths and a Lie' about work. Students write three statements about their jobs/skills (two true, one false). In pairs, they guess which is the lie. Teacher models first: 'I've worked in three countries (true), I can speak Japanese (false), I love Mondays (true)'.
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Find Someone Who...' worksheet with prompts like 'Find someone who has worked in a team', 'Find someone who can use Excel'.
Alternative 2: 'Mime the Job' - students mime a job (teacher, chef, engineer) and others guess.
pres: Presentation: Show a job ad for a 'Christmas Event Coordinator' on the board. Highlight key skills: 'organize events', 'work under pressure', 'communicate with clients'. Model interview Q&A: 'Why do you want this job?' 'I want to use my organizational skills to create memorable events.' Check understanding with 'thumbs up/down' for 'What skills are needed?'
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use a short video clip of a job interview, pausing to highlight phrases like 'My strength is...' and 'I'm looking for a challenge'.
Alternative 2: Bring in props (a phone, calendar, notepad) to demonstrate 'organize events' physically.
prac: Guided practice: 'Interview Match-Up' game. Students receive cards with interview questions (e.g., 'Tell me about your experience') and answers (e.g., 'I've organized three parties'). In pairs, they match them, then practice asking/answering. Teacher circulates to correct pronunciation.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Role Card Swap' - students get role cards (interviewer/interviewee) with sentence starters, then swap roles.
Alternative 2: 'Drill the Phrase' - choral repetition of key phrases like 'I'm good at...' and 'I've never...' with gestures.
ls: Listening slot: Play a PET-style audio of a job interview. Students listen and tick the skills mentioned (e.g., 'teamwork', 'problem-solving'). Replay to check answers, focusing on linking words like 'because' and 'for example'.
re: Reactivation game: 'Stand Up If...' - Teacher calls out skills (e.g., 'Stand up if you can cook!', 'Stand up if you've worked with a team!'). Students stand and share a brief example. Quick energy boost after the break.
prod: Production task: 'Mock Interview Pairs'. One student is the interviewer, the other is the interviewee for a 'Christmas Party Planner' role. They use the job ad and skills inventory to ask/answer questions for 5 minutes. Teacher notes language use for feedback.
rw: Reading and writing slot: Students read a short profile of 'Amina, Event Coordinator' and underline collocations like 'organize events' and 'meet deadlines'. Then, they write their own 80-word skills profile for a job application, using the model text.
st: Story/Song + Goodbye: Play a short video of 'The Story of Christmas as a Global Celebration' (2 mins). End with the goodbye routine: 'Today we practiced job interviews and Christmas vocabulary. Thank you, class! Have a great week!'
g: Cut job ads into sections; groups reassemble and match skills to requirements.
Students act out skills (e.g., 'typing', 'negotiating') for others to guess.
Bingo cards with phrases like 'I'm a team player'; students mark when they hear them.
Match invitation phrases ('Would you like to...?') with polite replies ('I'd love to, but...').
Students interview 3 different partners in 3 minutes about their dream job.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a full email accepting a Christmas party invitation with details.
Support / weaker learners: Use a sentence frame for their skills profile: 'I can... I have... I want...'
hw: Homework option 1: Record yourself doing a 2-minute mock interview and self-check using the class rubric.
Homework option 2: Write a polite email accepting or declining a Christmas party invitation (80 words).
Homework option 3: Find a job ad online and list 3 required skills and 2 qualities.
tip: Tip: For Moroccan learners, connect 'work' to local contexts like tourism or tech startups. Use 'Green March' or 'Labour Day' as examples of career-related celebrations to build cultural relevance.
